title: Anti-Sustainability Narratives in Chat Apps: What Shapes the Brazilian Far-Right Discussion About Socio-Environmental Issues on WhatsApp and Telegram
screen_reason: Observational analysis of 237,456 messages collected from 467 public WhatsApp groups and 136 Telegram groups/channels in Brazil (Jan 2023-Mar 2024). All domains shared more than 10 times were manually classified into 9 source types, and the paper reports the share of shared hyperlinks that were 'Junk News and Disinformation' (23,081 - 34.4% of total, 193 sites). That is a quantitative share of shared links carrying unreliable content, with a stated denominator class, so SHARING.

estimates.measure_type: % of hyperlinks shared in far-right Brazilian chat-app groups that pointed to junk news / disinformation websites
estimates.value_raw: Junk news and disinformation 23,081 - 34.4% of total (193 sites)
estimates.denominator: All classified hyperlinks shared in the in-scope socio-environmental messages from 467 WhatsApp groups and 136 Telegram groups/channels; the paper states 26,152 links from 2,226 domains were extracted and the 1,015 domains shared more than 10 times (24,179 links) were manually categorised. The total behind '34.4%' is not printed (23,081/0.344 implies ~67,100 link occurrences), so the denominator count is not fully reconcilable.
estimates.definition: The link's domain was manually classified as 'Junk News and Disinformation' - junk news in Howard's (2020) sense, hyperpartisan sites 'based on their frequent dissemination of misleading narratives, conspiracy theories, or highly distorted information'
estimates.misinfo_def: "Websites classified as junk news (Howard, 2020), carrying a hyperpartisan, mostly right-wing bias ... This classification is based on their frequent dissemination of misleading narratives, conspiracy theories, or highly distorted information, which undermines the quality of public debate and reinforces political polarization."
estimates.n: ~67,100 shared-link occurrences implied (23,081 junk-news links); 24,179 links from 1,015 domains were the manually categorised set
estimates.source_quote: Considering all messages with a hyperlink, Junk news and disinformation (23,081—34.4% of total), social media (22,418—33.4% of total), and minor news brands (16,283—24.2% of total) are overall the most shared types.
estimates.page_loc: pp. 15-17, section 'Disinformation and the Social Media Ecosystem' (also restated: '34.4% of shared links | 193 sites'); Methods p. 7-8
estimates.ground_truth_detail: The authors manually categorised every domain shared more than 10 times (1,015 domains) into 9 types, judging 'the content available on the linked pages, website interface and function, content production frequency, and the level of editorial professionalism (Santini et al., 2022)'. No inter-coder reliability statistic is reported and no external domain list is used.
estimates.moderator_quote: To identify the sources that underpin disinformation on sustainability, we extracted 26,152 shared links from 2226 domains found in messages relevant to the scope of our study. We manually categorized all domains shared more than 10 times (1015 in total, which amount to 24,179 links), classifying them into 9 types: (i) Junk News and Disinformation; ...
estimates.notes: Three caveats an adjudicator should weigh. (1) POPULATION: groups were purposively selected for far-right political content ('Groups were manually selected based on their focus on political discussion and related themes, primarily on far-right content'), so 34.4% describes a deliberately extreme subpopulation, not Brazilian WhatsApp/Telegram at large. (2) DENOMINATOR: the reported counts do not reconcile - 23,081 at 34.4% implies a total near 67,100, while the methods say 26,152 links were extracted and 24,179 categorised; the percentage is verbatim but the base is unclear (possibly link occurrences across messages rather than unique links). Hence confidence medium and borderline=true. (3) BREADTH: the numerator is a source-level 'junk news/hyperpartisan' judgement made by the authors themselves, not an item-level falsity check, so it is broader than 'false content'; breadth left blank per the source-level rule. Topic coded science_other for climate/environment; the corpus is topic-filtered to four socio-environmental issue areas. Data window spans Jan 2023-Mar 2024; year coded 2023 (most of the window).

missed_or_uncertain: (1) TOPIC-LEVEL disinformation shares from Figure 4 were not made into rows because they are topic subgroups of the extracted headline row: Attacks on MST 48.1% and Attacks on NGOs 48.6% junk-news/disinformation links (the highest), Conspiracy theories 22.6%, Ukraine War and fertilizers 11.3% (the lowest). The full 11.3%-48.6% range is worth reporting as definition/subsample sensitivity if the review wants it. (2) NOT extracted, judgement call for adjudication: the share of messages falling in the topic-model cluster 'Conspiracy theories' - 16.6% overall (32% on Telegram, 9.7% on WhatsApp). It is a thematic cluster produced by unsupervised BERTopic plus manual aggregation, NOT a truth/falsity judgement of each message (a message debunking or merely discussing a conspiracy theory would cluster there), so it fails the CONTENT ground-truth test as written. If the review counts conspiracy-topic classification as misinformation content, this is the row to add. (3) Other topic shares (Attacks on the Lula Government 35.9% Telegram / 29.6% WhatsApp; Attacks on MST 32.9% / 14.9%; In defense of agribusiness 26.1% / 1.5%; Attacks on NGOs 0.3% / 6.5%; Bolsonaro helped the environment 0.4% / 1.2%; Ukraine War and fertilizers 0.5% / 4.5%; Forest fire 0.2% / 3.1%) are thematic, not veracity, shares. (4) Other source-type shares (Social media 33.4%, Minor news brands 24.2%, Major news brands 6.1%) are the complement categories, not misinformation. (5) No CONCENTRATION figure (top X% of users or domains -> Y% of shares) is reported, though 193 junk-news sites are named as the most-shared category. (6) The 95% climate-awareness figure and the 40% source-corroboration figure are cited from CGEE (2024), not this study's data.

rob.design: Purposive, snowball-expanded monitoring panel of public far-right chat-app spaces: 467 WhatsApp groups (191,561 messages) and 136 Telegram groups/channels (45,895 messages), Jan 2023-Mar 2024, joined via invitation links found through targeted Google queries and links shared inside monitored groups; keyword query restricted content to four socio-environmental issue areas; non-Portuguese, very short and duplicate messages removed and 73,801 off-topic messages discarded by a first topic-modelling pass, leaving 87,968 messages; two-stage BERTopic (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 + UMAP + HDBSCAN) with research assistants manually aggregating topics; all domains shared >10 times manually classified into 9 source types; no inter-coder reliability reported for either the topic aggregation or the domain classification; no response-rate concept (observational trace data), and the sample is explicitly non-representative of the platforms' user base.
rob.item6_quote: Websites classified as junk news (Howard, 2020), carrying a hyperpartisan, mostly right-wing bias, often circulate in news lists that propagate conservative agendas and give voice to an anti-democratic opposition of the Lula government. This classification is based on their frequent dissemination of misleading narratives, conspiracy theories, or highly distorted information, which undermines the quality of public debate and reinforces political polarization.
rob.item10_quote: The predominance of Junk news and disinformation sites is evidence of this, which was the most shared category (34.4% of shared links | 193 sites).
